name: BLM Threatened and Endangered Species cooperative agreements
summary: US federal cooperative agreements with partners to conserve and recover threatened, endangered and sensitive species and their habitats on BLM-managed lands. Nonprofits and tribal organisations can apply; individuals cannot.

eligibility.rule: Not an individual or for-profit organization
Applicant is registered in SAM.gov before applying, unless applying as a natural person
Project is not under Idaho, Utah, NIFC or NOC
Project states a benefit to the public
Does not hire interns or crews under the Public Lands Corps Act of 1993

documents: SF-424A budget form, for non-construction projects
DOI R&D Current and Pending Support, for research projects
DOI R&D Biographical Sketch, for research projects
Negotiated indirect cost rate agreement, if previously negotiated
Conflict of interest disclosure, if applicable
Overlap or duplication of effort statement

geography.quote: to help inform a balance of multiple uses of BLM-managed lands

access.quote: Go to www.grants.gov to apply, track application status, and subscribe to updates.

window.quote: Posted date: August 11, 2026 Archive date: October 12, 2026

effort.quote: Before applying, all applicants except individuals applying as a natural person must be registered in SAM.gov.

Electronically submitted applications must be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m., ET, on the listed application due dates. Applications must be submitted through grants.gov. Applications will be reviewed, rated, ranked and selected via merit review committee. Open from August 11, 2026, through September 11, 2026.
During the eligibility review, the application is checked for timely submission, completed packages (see Application Documents above) and alignment with the requirements of this announcement.
Eligible applications will be evaluated in an objective and unbiased manner using the following merit review criteria:
Prior to making an award, the applicant will be assessed for their level of risk per 2 CFR 200.206.

eligibility.quote: Individuals and for-profit organizations are ineligible to apply for awards under this NOFO.
Before applying, all applicants except individuals applying as a natural person must be registered in SAM.gov.
Idaho, Utah, the National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC), and the National Operations Center (NOC) will not be accepting applications under this Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO).
All proposed projects submitted under this funding opportunity must state a benefit to the public.
This program NOFO does not support entities hiring interns or crews under the Public Lands Corps Act of 1993.

after_award.quote: Submit Federal Financial reports and Program Performance reports.

documents.quote: SF-424A, Budget Information - Non-Construction Programs Required for non-construction projects Page 8 of 20 Forms/Assurances/Certifications SF-LLL, Disclosure of Lobbying Activities Submission Requirement Required if requesting more than $100,000 in Federal funds and the applicant has used or plans to use funds other than Federal appropriated funds for lobbying related to the proposed project.

Project Abstract Summary (OMB 4040-0019). Must include, in plain language: • Award purpose, • Activities to be performed, Required from all applicants • Expected deliverables or outcomes, • Intended beneficiaries, Subrecipient activities (if known or specified at time of award) DOI Research and Development (R&D) - Current and Pending (Other) Support
DOI Research and Development (R&D) - Biographical Sketch
A Project Proposal must be submitted with the Standard Form (SF) 424 Application for Federal Assistance, for all BLM Assistance Agreements.
If your organization has previously negotiated a rate, attach a copy of the most recently negotiated rate agreement (active or expired).

If any actual or potential conflict of interest exists related to this project at the time of application, the applicant must provide sufficient information to support a program determination of significance per 2 CFR 1402.112.
Applicants must state in their application if the activities, costs, or time commitment of key personnel proposed in this application overlap with those in any other Federal proposal or award or not.
